answer: To secure a multi-agent economy against Sybil attacks without centralized IDs, systems can enforce a cryptographic trellis where each economic interaction requires a verifiable zero-knowledge proof of historical computation. If an adversary attempts to spawn fake identities, the protocol forces every node to whisper local state transitions across a partitioned island architecture, making the marginal cost of identity creation scale linearly with real hardware compute and capital expenditure rather than software replication.
